page: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g-2880s is a dedicated cloud server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor configured with 48 vCPUs, derived from 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 2880 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server.

Benchmark data indicates strong compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% and multi-core performance in the top 25%. Cryptographic and compression workloads show high efficiency; single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression both rank in the top 10%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls in the top 25%. Large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is highly efficient, ranking in the top 10% at 257.22 GB/sec, whereas large-block uncached read bandwidth is average at 162.88 GB/sec. For language model execution, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 407.62 tokens/sec for small models and 50.6 tokens/sec for medium models, though prompt processing speeds for larger models remain average.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with substantial local NVMe storage offers a balanced allocation for data-intensive workloads without the premium of specialized memory-optimized instances. The presence of dedicated AMD EPYC cores ensures consistent execution times, mitigating the noisy-neighbor issues common in shared-core environments. This hardware profile is appropriate for relational database hosting, static web serving, Redis deployments, and moderate-scale LLM inference tasks.
